$schema: application.context — runtime shape captured 2026-05-13 from a real Cloud Portal iframe (xmc:fullscreen extension point). Values redacted to placeholders; structure preserved verbatim. The blueprint's defensive layered render (FR-9, T023) must handle this exact shape, including the legacy `resources` / `touchpoints` duplicates of the canonical `resourceAccess` / `extensionPoints` arrays.
name: <app-display-name>
resources: [Legacy alias for resourceAccess — same array; ignore in new code per .d.ts canonical naming.]

resourceAccess.tenantDisplayName: <Human-readable tenant name e.g. 'CHAH DevEx Journey / PROD'>

touchpoints: [Legacy alias for extensionPoints — same array; ignore in new code.]

tenant_identity_key.decision: Use `application.context.marketplaceAppTenantId` as the PaywallGate's entitlement-key (tenants.tenant_id PK).
tenant_identity_key.rationale: It is the canonical Cloud Portal app-installation identifier — exactly what Cloud Portal sends in the iframe URL (?marketplaceAppTenantId=...) and what app-installation events would reference. One Cloud Portal installation = one paywall subscription is the simplest licensing model for v1. PRD-002+ can layer per-XM-Cloud-tenant licensing on top by also tracking `resourceAccess[].tenantId` if needed.
tenant_identity_key.alternative_considered_rejected: Use `resourceAccess[0].tenantId` (the XM Cloud tenant ID). Rejected because (a) an org may have multiple XM Cloud tenants under one app install, (b) `resourceAccess[]` could be empty if the app installation doesn't yet have an XM Cloud resource granted, (c) `marketplaceAppTenantId` is what Cloud Portal sends in the URL and is therefore the stable installation key.

tenant_display_name_chain.decision: For human-readable tenant labels (post-gate welcome screen), prefer `resourceAccess[0].tenantDisplayName`, fall back to `resourceAccess[0].tenantName` (often null), then to truncated `marketplaceAppTenantId` (last 8 chars), then to the literal 'your tenant'.
tenant_display_name_chain.rationale: Real-tenant capture showed `tenantName: null` but `tenantDisplayName: 'CHAH DevEx Journey / PROD'`. The architect's original FR-9 chain assumed `tenant.name` — wrong field entirely.

legacy_aliases.decision: Code reads from `resourceAccess` and `extensionPoints` (canonical .d.ts names). The legacy `resources` and `touchpoints` are tolerated as duplicate fields (same data, older naming) but not consumed.
legacy_aliases.rationale: Reduces ambiguity. The .d.ts is the contract; legacy duplicates exist for back-compat with older SDK consumers.
